title: A Familiar Baseball Field
description: Walk around a baseball field through familiar places, boundaries, and playing surfaces.
cardDescription: Walk around a baseball field through familiar places, boundaries, and playing surfaces.
focus: The clues identify where the game takes place. A few words name shapes or materials, while others name a position on the field.
solvingTip: Use location words such as center, edge, and beyond to separate the field features.
words: Infield shape formed by the four baseball bases
Raised area from which a baseball pitcher throws
One of the stations a runner must reach
Team seating area beside the playing field
Area where relief pitchers warm up
Part of the field around the bases
Green turf covering much of a baseball field
Loose earth covering parts of an infield
Describing ground outside the field’s fair boundaries
Straight marking defining a baseball field boundary
Barrier marking an outfield’s outer limit

answerNotes.DIAMOND: Diamond describes the arrangement of bases. The clue uses a field shape rather than a gemstone.
answerNotes.PLATE: Home plate is five-sided. Plate names a base here rather than a dish used for food.
answerNotes.DUGOUT: The dugout is a team’s seating area. It is separate from the bullpen used for warming up pitchers.
answerNotes.BULLPEN: A bullpen is associated with relief pitchers preparing to enter. The word does not refer to livestock in this setting.

title: In the Baseball Equipment Bag
description: Open an equipment bag with a crossword about familiar baseball gear and the parts players handle.
cardDescription: Open an equipment bag with a crossword about familiar baseball gear and the parts players handle.
focus: The clues describe objects by their shape or use. Some answers name a whole item, while others name a small part of one.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for equipment, clothing, or one feature of an object.
words: Long implement swung to hit a baseball
Round stitched object thrown and hit in baseball
Leather hand covering used to catch the ball
Catching glove with joined finger sections
Protective head covering worn by a batter
Soft headwear with a brim worn by a player
Stud on a baseball shoe for traction
Team shirt worn as part of a uniform
Band fastening baseball trousers at the waist
Narrow gripped end of a baseball bat
Thicker hitting section of a baseball bat
Raised stitched line on a baseball
Cord holding parts of a leather glove together
Flexible container holding a player’s equipment

answerNotes.MITT: A mitt has joined finger sections. A catcher’s mitt has a different shape from many fielding gloves.
answerNotes.BARREL: The barrel is the thicker bat section. Handle names the narrower portion held by the batter.
answerNotes.CLEAT: Cleat names one shoe stud here. The plural cleats can also refer to the shoes themselves.
answerNotes.SEAM: The seam is the stitched line on the ball. The clue identifies a surface feature rather than the whole ball.

title: Between Pitch and Hit
description: Follow familiar baseball actions through words for throwing, batting, and running.
cardDescription: Follow familiar baseball actions through words for throwing, batting, and running.
focus: These clues define actions and short play descriptions. They do not ask for player records or historical statistics.
solvingTip: Notice whether the clue describes the pitcher, batter, runner, or fielder.
words: To throw the ball toward the batter
To move the bat in an attempt to hit
To meet the ball softly with a held-out bat
Fair batted ball that lets the batter reach safely without an error or fielder's choice
To secure a ball before it reaches the ground
To send the ball through the air with the arm
To reach a base by lowering and gliding along the ground
To advance a base while the defense is not handling a batted ball
To touch a runner with a held ball to attempt an out
Award allowing a batter to reach first after four balls
A batter's swing and miss, for example
Batted ball sent outside the fair boundaries
Result that removes a batter or runner from play

answerNotes.BUNT: A bunt uses a held-out bat to meet the ball softly. It differs from a full swing.
answerNotes.WALK: Walk is a baseball award here. The word does not simply describe moving on foot.
answerNotes.TAG: Tag is a touching action in this clue. The ball must be held for the ordinary tagging play described.
answerNotes.STEAL: Steal has a sporting meaning for advancing a base. The clue does not describe taking someone’s property.

title: Reading the Ballpark Scoreboard
description: Read familiar baseball scoring words without needing a famous game’s statistics.
cardDescription: Read familiar baseball scoring words without needing a famous game’s statistics.
focus: The clues name results, game divisions, and recorded events. Short words can have a specific baseball meaning.
solvingTip: Look for a result, a counted event, or a stage of play rather than a person’s name.
words: Game division giving each team a chance to bat
Unit added to a baseball team’s score
Batter's credited safe reach on a fair ball, excluding an error or fielder's choice
Fielding mistake recorded in a baseball score
Total runs credited to a team
Team playing at its own ballpark
Team visiting the other club’s ballpark
First half of a baseball inning
Second half of a baseball inning
Hit on which the batter reaches first base
Hit on which the batter reaches second base
Hit on which the batter reaches third base
Informal name for a home run
Equal run totals for the two teams

answerNotes.INNING: An inning is divided into a top and a bottom. Visitors bat in the top and the home team in the bottom; the final bottom half is not always needed.
answerNotes.ERROR: Error names a recorded fielding mistake. Not every unsuccessful play is automatically scored as an error.
answerNotes.HOMER: Homer is a familiar short form of home run. The clue uses a baseball result rather than a person’s name.
answerNotes.DOUBLE: A double credits a two-base hit. It identifies the hit result rather than two separate singles.

title: From a Seat in the Stands
description: Enjoy a spectator’s view through words for ballpark seating, snacks, and cheering.
cardDescription: Enjoy a spectator’s view through words for ballpark seating, snacks, and cheering.
focus: The clues stay with the fan experience around the field. Some words name objects or places; others describe a sound or action.
solvingTip: Use the seat, snack, and sound clues as different routes into the grid.
words: Person following and supporting a baseball team
Seating sections around a playing field
An uncovered bench seat at a sports ground
Proof of paid admission to a ballgame
Worker who helps spectators find their ballpark seats
Line of spectator seats at a stadium
To call out support for a team
To applaud a good play with the hands
Small shelled snack often associated with ballparks
Twisted baked snack sold at many stadiums
Carbonated drink bought at a ballpark concession stand
Printed guide to teams or events at a game

answerNotes.FAN: Fan means an enthusiastic supporter here. It does not name a device that moves air.
answerNotes.BLEACHER: A bleacher is an uncovered bench seat. Bleachers commonly names the larger bank of such seating.
answerNotes.AISLE: Aisle is the passage, not the seat. The silent letters help distinguish its spelling from isle.
answerNotes.VENDOR: A vendor sells goods. The clue identifies the seller rather than one particular snack.
